subject.title: Unhandled socket error in SSRF fetch wrapper can kill the gateway process (IPv6-only DNS + Happy Eyeballs)

question: Should the SSRF socket-error fix land by repairing https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100433, or should maintainers replace it with a new owner-authored security-boundary patch?
rationale: The issue is valid at source level, but the current candidate touches SSRF and Undici contracts and lacks live proof, so the landing path needs security-boundary ownership.

options.title: Repair linked PR
options.body: Preserve DNS pinning and explicit-proxy contracts, add live IPv6-unreachable proof, and merge the linked PR only after review clears.

options.title: Replace with maintainer patch
options.body: Pause or close the linked PR and implement the same rejection behavior in a new security-reviewed patch if the connector design is not salvageable.

recommendation.title: Repair linked PR
recommendation.body: Preserve DNS pinning and explicit-proxy contracts, add live IPv6-unreachable proof, and merge the linked PR only after review clears.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent and historical ownership signal for this SSRF guarded-fetch path.
